title: Accessibility Maturity Models & Roadmaps 🗺️
description: Assess your organization's a11y maturity, define a roadmap, and measure progress with KPIs.

slides.title: Where Are You on the Maturity Curve? 📊
slides.content:
Accessibility maturity models help you understand your current state and chart a path forward. Common stages:

- **Stage 0: Unaware** – no knowledge, no effort.
- **Stage 1: Reactive** – fix issues after complaints or lawsuits.
- **Stage 2: Compliant** – meet minimum WCAG AA on key pages.
- **Stage 3: Proactive** – accessibility integrated into process, training.
- **Stage 4: Innovative** – inclusive design drives innovation, a11y is a competitive advantage.

Most organizations are somewhere between Reactive and Proactive.

quizData.question: An organization that only fixes accessibility bugs when a user complains is at which maturity stage?
quizData.explanation: Reactive stage involves addressing issues only after external pressure.

slides.title: Assessing Your Organization 🔍
slides.content:
Use a structured assessment:

- **People**: training, awareness, roles.
- **Process**: how a11y is integrated into design, dev, testing, procurement.
- **Technology**: tooling, automated tests, component libraries.
- **Content**: documents, videos, third‑party embeds.

Conduct interviews, survey teams, and review past audits. Be honest – identify gaps without blame.

quizData.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension typically assessed in a maturity model?
quizData.explanation: Revenue is not an accessibility maturity metric.

slides.title: Creating a Roadmap 🗺️
slides.content:
Based on the assessment, define a phased roadmap:

- **Quick wins**: fix critical automated issues, add skip link, color contrast.
- **Build capacity**: train team, establish champions, set up CI checks.
- **Systemic changes**: implement design system updates, procurement criteria, VPATs.
- **Innovation**: user research with disabled participants, co‑design, publish thought leadership.

Set SMART goals: e.g., 'Achieve 0 critical axe violations on all pages by Q2'.

quizData.question: What is a good first step in an accessibility roadmap after a maturity assessment?

options.text: Address critical automated issues and provide basic training

quizData.explanation: Quick wins build momentum and trust.

slides.title: KPIs & Metrics 📊
slides.content:
Measure what matters:

- **Automated violations count** over time (trending down).
- **Manual audit findings** per release.
- **Training completion rate**.
- **User‑reported a11y bugs**.
- **Accessibility score** (Lighthouse or similar) on key pages.
- **VPAT completion** for products.

Track and report regularly to leadership. Transparency accelerates progress.

slides.title: Maturity Frameworks to Explore 📚
slides.content:
- **W3C Accessibility Maturity Model** (draft).
- **IAAP Maturity Model**.

Use an established model to benchmark against industry peers.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't aim for perfection in year one
Focus on incremental improvement. Celebrate small wins, and keep the momentum.
